summary: Phase 149O.20L.1A -- HMRC-001 v1.1 HMIC Contract-Identity Alignment Repair: narrow identity-alignment repair only, addressing progression blocker B-149O.20L.1-1. Phase 149O.20L.1 amended HMRC-001 from v1.0 to v1.1 without touching HMIC-001 (explicitly out of scope for that phase), leaving HMIC-001's own header 'Depends on' line stale -- it still claimed HMRC-001 v1.0, byte-unchanged. Independently reconstructed (not assumed from any prior phase's report) both the pre-149O.20L.1 baseline, via git show at the true 149O.20L.1 phase-entry commit f14e524e (HMRC-001 v1.0, HMIC-001's Depends-on line v1.0 -- internally consistent), and the post-149O.20L.1, pre-repair mismatch, via git show at 149O.20L.1's own final commit 90e14496 (HMRC-001 live at v1.1, HMIC-001's header still v1.0 -- a genuine divergence, confirmed as a direct, sole consequence of 149O.20L.1, not a pre-existing defect and not evidence 149O.20K/149O.20K.1/149O.20K.2/149O.20K.3 were ever inconsistent when completed). Determined Outcome B via direct source reading: HMIC-REQ-067 (contract Section 20) names HMRC-001 as a contract_versions family member by Contract ID only, with no version-number literal anywhere in its normative text; HMIC-REQ-069 independently requires contract_versions validation to compare each entry against 'the named contract's own current, live version header' -- i.e. the contract's own normative mechanism is designed to track the live document dynamically, never to freeze a version number in prose. Production's derive_contract_versions (core/hatp_mandatory_certification.py) was directly exercised against the live repository before any edit this phase made: it already returned {'HMRC-001': '1.1', ...}, correctly reflecting the live v1.1 document, with no stale literal anywhere in its implementation (_CONTRACT_IDENTITY_FILES stores (contract_id, path) pairs, never (contract_id, version) pairs). Conclusion: neither HMIC-REQ-067's normative text nor production's derive_contract_versions mechanism was ever stale; the sole defect was this document's own descriptive Depends-on header line -- a summary field structurally parallel to the Version:/Status: header fields above it, not a normative requirement body, and distinct from the illustrative, deliberately non-synchronized four-member contract_versions example under an earlier schema section (already left un-updated in place across the v1.2 and v1.3 amendments, an established prior disposition this phase does not disturb). Repaired in place, same version (HMIC-001 stays v1.3, mirroring the 149O.20D.1 same-version-repair precedent, which repaired a disclosed gap in place without a version bump): updated the header Status line to name this repair; added a new Repaired by: Phase 149O.20L.1A header line; corrected the Depends-on line to HMRC-001 v1.1 (all other four members -- HATP-001, HSCE-001, RAE-001, HBDC-001 -- unchanged) and reworded its label from '(unamended, byte-unchanged)' to '(current, HMIC-unamended)' to remove the now-inaccurate byte-unchanged claim while preserving the true claim that HMIC-001 itself did not amend any of the five dependency contracts; added new contract Section 54 ('Contract Repair History -- Phase 149O.20L.1A (Finding B-149O.20L.1-1)') documenting the finding, both reconstructed states, the Outcome-B mechanism proof, the exact repair delta, scope-discipline confirmation, and the verdict, following the same section shape as Section 52's (149O.20D.1) same-version repair precedent. During drafting, two self-inflicted naive-text-matching collisions were found and fixed before finalizing: (1) the header's new Repaired-by line initially cited 'HMIC-REQ-069' by name, which -- because it appears earlier in the document than Section 20's real HMIC-REQ-069 definition -- caused two pre-existing proximity-based tests (test_id_version_content_three_way_binding_all_visible, test_version_drift_still_text_mandated_as_contract_mismatch) to search from the wrong occurrence and fail; reworded to 'this contract's own Section 20 live-header-comparison mechanism' without repeating the literal requirement ID, restoring both tests to their correct pre-existing state; (2) Section 54.1's initial prose quoted HRMC-001's own header value using the exact literal markdown token '**Version:** 1.1', which coincidentally satisfied four unrelated pre-existing naive substring tests (test_contract_id_and_version_frozen, test_contract_version_remains_1_0, test_contract_version_is_v1_1, test_contract_status_header_reflects_v1_1_pending_verification) that intend to check HMIC-001's own version, not HMRC-001's -- reworded to prose description without the literal markdown token, restoring all four to their correct (expected-failing, historical-pin) state. Scope discipline confirmed: no HMIC-REQ-### text added, removed, or narrowed; HMIC-REQ-067's five-member contract_versions family list is unchanged (same five members, same order); no HMRC-001 byte touched (HMRC-001 remains v1.1, exactly as 149O.20L.1 left it); no Class-B verifier module touched; HMIC-001's twenty-eight-file source-scope target and production's current twenty-eight-file/five-contract identity (both already aligned since 149O.20K.2/149O.20K.3, independently reconfirmed unchanged by this phase) are both unaffected; verify_class_b_deployment_conformance remains uncalled by any readiness or certification path; hatp_mandatory_cutover.py remains the unwired seven-term production readiness vector; no certification, activation, or Class-B provisioning occurred. New 33-test module (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_1a_hmrc_v1_1_hmic_contract_identity_alignment_repair.py) independently re-derives, from git history (not trusting this phase's own report), the pre-149O.20L.1 consistency, the post-149O.20L.1 mismatch, the Outcome-B mechanism proof (including a fail-closed-proof construction demonstrating a stale-v1.0-expectation would genuinely mismatch live state and the repaired v1.1-expectation matches exactly), the repaired header state, five-member family preservation, HMRC-001 byte-identity, source-scope and Class-B-binding preservation, zero readiness-path consumer, and CBV-S1/CBV-S10 status language -- all 33 pass. Established a fixed pre-phase baseline via an isolated git worktree at the true entry commit (90e14496, 149O.20L.1's own final commit); ran full fast_green (-n auto) on the isolated baseline (144 failed / 6964 passed / 5 skipped / 10 errors) and on the current working tree across three passes: a pre-commit working-tree pass, a post-commit pass, and a final stable post-commit re-measurement. Performed exact sorted node-ID diffs (never count-only) at each pass. The pre-commit working-tree diff initially showed both false-positive apparent 'fixes' (the four/two naive-substring collisions above, corrected before committing) and eleven genuine new failures (all fixed-commit self-checks or git-status-porcelain working-tree-dirty checks any HMIC-001 edit necessarily triggers) plus the already-known test_shell_gate.py::TestAuditPersistence::test_audit_verify_cli environmental flake (independently reproduced passing in isolation, unrelated to this phase, previously documented by 149O.20L.1's own report). After committing, the working-tree-dirty-style checks (eleven of the thirteen pre-commit-only deltas) resolved back to passing since the tree was clean again; the final stable post-commit diff shows exactly 2 new-vs-baseline node deltas, both individually re-run and classified: test_phase_149o_20d_hmic_v1_2_hbdc_bound_contract_identity_evolution.py::test_depends_on_line_lists_hbdc (a genuine, expected consequence of the Depends-on line's label rewording -- a 149O.20D-era test pinned to the old exact label text) and test_phase_149o_20k_3_hmic_class_b_verifier_production_source_set_alignment_independent_verification.py::TestByteIdentitySinceK2Entry::test_hmic_contract_byte_unchanged_since_k2_entry (a fixed-commit self-check comparing HMIC-001 against its 149O.20K.2-entry commit -- any future HMIC-001 edit necessarily breaks it, the same documented class as every prior HMIC-001-touching phase). A separately-observed test_phase_149o_20i_hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py::test_interpreter_check_fixture_agent_unwritable failure during one xdist run was independently reproduced passing in isolation -- confirmed as the same documented -n-auto shared-mutable-state flake class, unrelated to this phase's file changes. Zero unexplained or unclassified new failures. A broad -k 'hmrc or hmic or contract_versions or 20l' sweep on both baseline and current tree found exactly 6 new deltas, all a strict subset of the fast_green-classified set. Clean-deselected primary citation (156-node argv-list --deselect via Python subprocess argv, never shell string interpolation, sourced from the exact post-commit run being cited): 0 failed, 6995 passed, 5 skipped, 1 pre-existing fido2 collection error. B-149O.20L.1-1: REPAIRED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING -- NOT CLOSED. CBV-S1 unaffected, remains at its scoped closure boundary exactly as before (HMIC-001 v1.3, production 28/5, not reopened). CBV-S10 unaffected, remains OPEN -- READINESS CONTRACT EVOLVED -- HMIC CONTRACT-IDENTITY REALIGNMENT IN PROGRESS/COMPLETE -- INDEPENDENT READINESS CONTRACT VERIFICATION + PRODUCTION INTEGRATION PENDING. Class-B remains NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable, unchanged throughout. Recommended next phase: Phase 149O.20L.1B -- HMRC-001 v1.1 HMIC Contract-Identity Alignment Independent Verification (not begun by this phase). L.2 not begun.
